📚 Today you learned

Position Concentration Risk

Your GOOG position is a good case study in why concentration has to be measured two ways. Against invested capital alone, GOOG is 52.2% — well past your 15–18% max-position rule if you only looked at that number. But against total net liq ($535.68 as of the last verified snapshot), it's only ~20.6%, because cash is 61.7% of the account. The rule exists to cap how much a single name can hurt your whole account, not just your "at risk" sleeve — so the net-liq number is the one that actually matters for risk sizing. This is also why the position-sizing rule always reads "% of total portfolio value," not "% of invested capital": a concentrated bet inside a mostly-cash account is a very different risk than the same concentration in a fully-invested one. Today's GOOG stop question is a live test of that math — even in the bad-case scenario, a full stop-out only touches ~20% of the account, not half of it.

Also today: Cash cushion ratio — cash ÷ net liq; the higher it is, the more a single position's stop can go wrong before it threatens the account, not just the trade.
